overview.title: 📖 Overview: The Line Between the Sun's Heat and the Fire's Heat
overview.subtitle: Shabbat 39a–39b
overview.hebrewSource: בְּחַמָּה — דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דִּשְׁרֵי. בְּתוֹלְדוֹת הָאוּר — כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דַּאֲסִיר
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: Continuing from the mishna's rules about soaking and rinsing salted fish, the Gemara turns to a subtler question: is heat that comes from the sun treated like heat from fire? Rav Nachman lays out the three-way distinction — direct sunlight, derivatives of fire, and derivatives of the sun — and the Gemara tests it against an egg rolled in warm sand, a hot rooftop, and the famous incident of the Tiberias hot-water pipe, whose true source of heat turns out to be a matter of dispute. The daf closes with the related question of how one may wash after Shabbat with water heated the day before.

slides.title: 🌞 Rav Nachman's Three-Way Distinction
slides.subtitle: Sunlight, fire-derivatives, and sun-derivatives are not all treated alike

nodes.content: ❓ Is heating food with the sun's warmth the same as cooking it with fire?

columns.label: Direct sunlight
columns.content: Everyone agrees: permitted. This is not fire, not real cooking

columns.label: Derivatives of fire
columns.content: Everyone agrees: forbidden, exactly like fire itself

nodes.content: ⚖️ Derivatives of the sun (e.g. sun-warmed cloths or sand): The Rabbis decree against it, lest people confuse it with derivatives of fire. Rabbi Yosei sees no need for such a decree

slides.title: 🥚 Two Reasons Not to Roll an Egg in Sand
slides.subtitle: Rabba and Rav Yosef disagree on why — tested by a hot rooftop

lines.speaker: Rabba
lines.text: The Sages forbade insulating an egg in sun-warmed sand as a decree — lest one come to insulate it in hot ashes instead, which is truly forbidden.

lines.speaker: Rav Yosef
lines.text: No — the real reason is that insulating displaces the dirt, which resembles digging.

lines.speaker: Test case
lines.text: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel permits rolling an egg on a hot roof but forbids it on hot lime. On Rabba's reasoning, a roof is nothing like ash — no decree needed.

lines.speaker: Same result
lines.text: And on Rav Yosef's reasoning too: a typical roof has no loose dirt to displace, so no prohibition applies there either.

callout.label: Where they truly differ:
callout.text: Only with loose earth — which involves no 'digging' — does the practical difference emerge: Rav Yosef would permit it, Rabba would still forbid it.

slides.title: 😈 Why the Tiberias Hot Springs Don't Prove Rabbi Yosei Wrong
slides.subtitle: The Rabbis' challenge, and Rabbi Yosei's answer
slides.hebrewSource: הַהוּא תּוֹלְדוֹת אוּר הוּא, דְּחָלְפִי אַפִּיתְחָא דְגֵיהִנָּם
slides.label: The exchange:
slides.text: The Rabbis challenged Rabbi Yosei: the people of Tiberias ran cold water through hot springs — a derivative of the sun, since no fire heated it directly — and yet the Sages forbade using that water. Doesn't that show even sun-derivatives are prohibited? Rabbi Yosei answered that the comparison fails: Tiberias's hot springs are not sun-derivatives at all. They are, in fact, derivatives of fire, because the water passes over the mouth of Gehenna itself and is heated by that subterranean fire — an entirely different category from ordinary sun-warmed water.

slides.title: 🛁 May One Rinse the Whole Body With Water Heated Before Shabbat?
slides.subtitle: Three tannaim, and the halakha that emerges

boxes.title: Rabbi Meir
items: Applies to both hot and cold water
No exception for water heated before Shabbat

boxes.title: Rabbi Shimon
items: Since the water was heated before Shabbat began
The mishna's unattributed ruling follows this view

boxes.title: Rabbi Yehuda
items: Rabbi Yochanan rules the halakha follows this view

summary.principle: Not all indirect heat is equal: the sun's direct warmth is always permitted, true fire-derivatives are always forbidden, and the disputed middle category of sun-derivatives depends on whether the heat source, like Tiberias's springs, is secretly a derivative of fire after all.

flowSteps.content: 🐟 Salted fish may be soaked if pre-heated, only rinsed if not — except fish where rinsing itself completes cooking
🌞 Rav Nachman: direct sun always permitted, fire-derivatives always forbidden, sun-derivatives disputed
🥚 Rabba (decree vs. ash) and Rav Yosef (displacing dirt) diverge only over loose earth

columns.content: 😈 Tiberias's springs are ruled fire-derivatives, since they pass the mouth of Gehenna
🛁 Halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda: hot water forbidden, cold water permitted for rinsing

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: the Sages consistently guard against confusing permitted indirect heat with forbidden fire-based cooking

quiz.q: According to the mishna, for which foods does even rinsing in hot water on Shabbat constitute forbidden cooking?
o: Fresh vegetables
Old salted fish and kolias ha'ispanin
Any bread product
Dairy foods only
quiz.e: The mishna singles out old salted fish and kolias ha'ispanin (a Spanish fish) as items for which rinsing itself completes the cooking process, like a slightly-cooked egg.

quiz.q: According to Rav Nachman, on which category of heat do the Rabbis and Rabbi Yosei actually disagree?
o: Direct sunlight
Derivatives of fire
Derivatives of the sun
Cooking with salt
quiz.e: Everyone agrees direct sun is permitted and fire-derivatives are forbidden; the dispute is specifically about sun-derivatives, like sun-warmed sand or cloths.

quiz.q: What is the practical difference between Rabba's and Rav Yosef's reasons for forbidding insulating an egg in sand?
o: There is no practical difference at all
Loose earth — permitted under Rav Yosef's reasoning (no digging involved), still forbidden under Rabba's decree
Whether the egg is raw or already cooked
Whether the sand is wet or dry
quiz.e: Rabba's decree (against confusing it with hot ashes) still applies to loose earth, while Rav Yosef's reason (displacing dirt, like digging) does not apply where there is nothing to displace.

quiz.q: How does Rabbi Yosei answer the challenge that the Tiberias hot springs prove sun-derivatives are forbidden?
o: He concedes the point and retracts his opinion
He argues the springs are actually derivatives of fire, since they pass over the mouth of Gehenna
He says Tiberias water was never actually forbidden
He claims the incident never happened
quiz.e: Rabbi Yosei explains that the Tiberias springs are heated by the fires of Gehenna, making them true fire-derivatives rather than sun-derivatives.

quiz.q: According to Rabbi Yochanan, whose opinion does the halakha follow regarding rinsing the whole body with water heated before Shabbat?
o: Rabbi Meir, forbidding it entirely
Rabbi Shimon, permitting it entirely
Rabbi Yehuda — hot water forbidden, cold water permitted
None of the three; the question remains open
quiz.e: Rabbi Yochanan rules that the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda: cold water may be used to rinse the whole body, but hot water may not.
